name: Fontan-associated liver disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No formal consensus criteria; diagnosis based on clinical, imaging, and histological findings in post-Fontan patients

criteria.description: History of Fontan procedure for single ventricle physiology
Evidence of hepatic fibrosis or cirrhosis on liver biopsy or elastography
Imaging findings consistent with hepatic venous congestion and fibrosis (e.g., ultrasound, MRI, elastography)
Elevated liver function tests (transaminases, bilirubin) supportive but not diagnostic
Clinical signs of portal hypertension such as splenomegaly or varices

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: History of Fontan procedure plus evidence of hepatic fibrosis or cirrhosis on biopsy or elastography and compatible imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multidisciplinary evaluation including cardiology and hepatology

laboratory: Mild to moderate elevation of ALT and AST
imaging: Ultrasound showing heterogeneous liver echotexture and hepatomegaly
MRI demonstrating hepatic fibrosis and congestion
Transient elastography indicating increased liver stiffness
Doppler ultrasound showing altered hepatic venous flow
other: Liver biopsy showing sinusoidal dilation, fibrosis, and congestion
Hemodynamic studies confirming elevated central venous pressure

distinguishingFeatures: Occurs secondary to right heart failure without Fontan physiology
Absence of congenital heart disease and Fontan circulation
No history of Fontan surgery or elevated central venous pressure

redFlags: Rapid progression of liver fibrosis or cirrhosis
Development of portal hypertension complications such as variceal bleeding
Signs of hepatocellular carcinoma on imaging or biopsy
